builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Towards Autoregressive Neural Network Parameter Generation
summary: IGPG replaces random or task-specific weight initialization by quantizing pretrained network weights with a VQ-VAE and training a prefix-conditioned autoregressive generator to synthesize new parameters token-by-token. The cost is a full generative pipeline: a collection of pretrained models to learn from, VQ-VAE training, autoregressive training over weight tokens, and a subsequent adaptation or fine-tuning stage before the generated weights are usable. It can fail because the generated parameters are only initializations that still require adaptation, generalization to out-of-distribution architectures remains limited, and quantization plus generative mismatch can yield weights that underperform standard transfer learning from an existing pretrained checkpoint.
rationale: The method requires a corpus of pretrained models, VQ-VAE training, and autoregressive generator training to produce weights for other tasks, which neither matches the reader's production inference workload nor fits a constrained compute budget.
technique: Autoregressive generation of neural network weights via VQ-VAE tokenization

claims.statement: IGPG replaces random or task-specific weight initialization by quantizing pretrained network weights with a VQ-VAE and training a prefix-conditioned autoregressive generator to synthesize new parameters token-by-token. The cost is a full generative pipeline: a collection of pretrained models to learn from, VQ-VAE training, autoregressive training over weight tokens, and a subsequent adaptation or fine-tuning stage before the generated weights are usable. It can fail because the generated parameters are only initializations that still require adaptation, generalization to out-of-distribution architectures remains limited, and quantization plus generative mismatch can yield weights that underperform standard transfer learning from an existing pretrained checkpoint.

Generated parameters provide useful initializations for held-out datasets and architectures, improving downstream performance over random initialization after adaptation; no quantitative factor is reported.
